Une étude de l’Agence algérienne de prom: A study by the Algerian Investment Promotion Agency (AAPI) reveals that Algiers could replace 95% of its industrial imports ($38.86 billion/year) with local production. A major strategy to reduce hydrocarbon dependence and boost national industry.
L’Agence algérienne de promotion de l’in: The Algerian Investment Promotion Agency (AAPI) publishes an analysis in Investment DZ (August 2026): 95% of annual industrial imports ($36.87 billion out of $38.86 billion) could be covered by national production. Based on 10 years of data (2014–2024), this study identifies 144 priority industrial branches to reduce import dependence and diversify exports. Key sectors include agri-food, pharmaceuticals, industrial equipment, construction materials, and food processing, with a substitution potential estimated at $6.5 billion for the agri-food sector alone. The objective? To develop an integrated industrial base and strengthen the competitiveness of Algerian products on international markets.
Cette analyse s’inscrit dans le cadre de: This analysis is part of AAPI's strategy to direct investments toward high value-added activities.
L’étude recense 673 lignes tarifaires ré: The study identifies 673 tariff lines spread across 11 sectors and 144 industrial branches, with potential for import substitution and export diversification. Among the priority sectors are agri-food, pharmaceuticals, industrial equipment, construction materials, and food processing. These sectors offer major opportunities to reduce import dependence and boost local exports. The goal is to create an autonomous local industry while meeting the needs of the national market.
L’AAPI souligne que l’Algérie dispose d’: AAPI emphasizes that Algeria has major assets: availability of raw materials, competitive production costs, and local skills. These factors enable the development of an industry capable of meeting national needs and exporting. However, this transition requires targeted investments and an ambitious industrial policy to support economic diversification. The agency insists on the progressive reduction of dependence on hydrocarbons, a historically dominant sector, toward higher value-added activities. The ultimate goal: historical industrial autonomy and export diversification.
Ces facteurs combinés offrent une base s: These combined factors provide a solid foundation for developing a local industry capable of meeting national market needs while exporting.
Avec cette étude, l’Algérie s’engage dan: With this study, Algeria is embarking on a major industrial revolution, reducing its dependence on hydrocarbons and strengthening its global competitiveness.
